title: Arkret Device Pairing Short-Link DTOs
description: Closed request and response DTOs for the server-mediated device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). These endpoints are unauthenticated: staging mints an account-less pending record, and resolve/status exchange the short handle for pairing material without binding or granting anything until an authenticated device authorizes the pairing.

algorithm_list.description: Algorithm ids supported by the target device, sorted by UTF-8 bytewise order and deduplicated before they enter any transcript.

pairing_nonce.description: base64url CSPRNG nonce carrying at least 128 bits of entropy.

gate_audience_uri.description: Origin of the Account Authority gate surface (gate_account_base_url) this pairing request is bound to. Minted by the staging service; the target proof commits to it so a proof cannot be replayed against another Account Authority.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey shape shared with agent-operations. For a staged device the key material is carried in `key` and `kid` is the target `ak:device:<uuid>` id.

device_pairing_state.description: Lifecycle state of a staged device-pairing short-link record. A staged record starts pending_authorization, flips to authorized once an authenticated device completes ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1, and reports expired once its bounded TTL has elapsed.

device_pairing_stage_request_body.description: Unauthenticated stage request that mints a fresh account-less pending pairing record. It carries only the canonical public key and a client nonce: the target proof cannot exist yet, because it must commit to the request id, pairing code, expiry, gate audience and server nonce that this call mints. It also deliberately omits hpke_key and algorithms; those reach the approving device inside the signed device_pairing_target_proof over the out-of-band channel, so the anonymous staging surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint. The record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it.

device_pairing_stage_outcome.description: Server-minted challenge inputs for the sole target proof. request id and pairing code are body-only anonymous lookup credentials; they MUST NOT enter URL path/query.

device_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for device-pairing short-link handoff. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

device_pairing_bootstrap.description: Anonymous challenge inputs used to independently recompute the staged challenge digest before checking the out-of-band target proof. Contains no target proof, HPKE key or algorithm fingerprint. No authorization is granted.

device_pairing_status_request_body.description: Body-only poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found).

device_pairing_status_outcome.description: Authorization status for a staged device-pairing record. While the record is still open, state is pending_authorization. Once an authenticated device has authorized this pairing, state is authorized and device_id plus authorized_event_ref are present. An open record whose bounded TTL has elapsed reports state expired.

authorized_event_ref.description: Accepted ak.device.authorize Event id. It is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.4.1: before the target device assembles the identity locally it MUST fetch this Event and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key_did, hpke_key and algorithms, and an expected complete AccountId, or fail closed.

device_pairing_target_proof.description: The single target possession proof for staged accepted_device pairing. Sign UTF8("ak.device_authorize_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1\n") || JCS(all fields except device_signature). The unsigned challenge digest is independently recomputed from the server record; the signed descriptor covers target key, HPKE key, algorithms and binding kind. Only token plus this proof travel out of band; anonymous stage/resolve MUST NOT receive the proof. Approved Event retains the descriptor and challenge digest so its signature remains re-verifiable after stage cleanup.

device_public_key_did.description: Self-describing did:key form of the same Ed25519 key as new_device_pubkey.key. A verifier MUST reject an proof whose device_public_key_did decodes to different key bytes than the staged or forwarded new_device_pubkey.

hpke_key.description: Target device X25519 HPKE public key. This proof is its authority; a service MUST NOT supply or substitute it.

authorization_binding_kind.description: This transcript exists only for accepted_device pairing. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery use their separate full possession objects, and a transcript from one binding kind MUST NOT be accepted for another.

pairing_challenge_transcript_digest.description: SHA-256 of the domain-separated canonical staged challenge bytes defined in device-lifecycle.md 2.1.2. Verifiers independently reconstruct it from bootstrap/server stage. Covers request id, code, audience, expiry, both nonces, staged key and metadata digest; never accepts a caller-self-reported challenge.

device_signature.description: Ed25519 signature by the private key of device_public_key_did over the canonical signing input above. The approving device MUST copy it byte-for-byte into device_authorize_payload.device_signature and into the pair_device request device_signature.
